newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt sees '97 budget deficit 2.6 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt sees '97 budget deficit 2.6 pct GDP.

text.p: The Swedish government, releasing its 1997 budget on Friday, forecast its budget deficit at 2.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 compared to a forecast of 2.7 percent at an April budget.
This falls below the Maastricht Treaty's target of a deficit of three percent of GDP in 1997, the key year for deciding which countries quality for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
The government forecast state borrowing requirement totalling 2.4 percent of GDP in 1996, 3.1 percent in 1997 and 0.3 percent in 1998.
It said the budget deficit would be 4.0 percent of GDP in 1996, improving to a surplus of 2.3 percent of GDP in 2000.
"The improvement is largely due to a falling expenditure in relationship to GDP," the government said in its budget.
